 Order
1. With the consent of learned counsel for the parties matter is finally heard.

2. This appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 has been preferred by the claimant/appellant being aggrieved by the award dated 3.3.2016 passed in Claim Case No.309/2014 by 16th Member, MACT, Indore, whereby a total sum of Rs.38,55,436/- has been awarded to him by way of compensation along with interest at the rate of 6% against the amount of Rs.1,50,00,000/- as claimed before the claims tribunal.

3. Facts of the case in short are that on 3.11.2014 around 12.30 AM, the present appellant met with an accident, which was driven by non-applicant No.1 rashly and negligently as a result, the claimant sustained grievous injuries including permanent disabilities of 75% on head.
On account of the accident the claim case was preferred by the claimant and a trial was set into a motion.
The learned tribunal has found that the accident was caused due to rash and negligent driving of respondent No.1 / driver.

The offending vehicle was registered in the NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2026:MPHC-IND:3439 2 MA-1738-2016 name of respondent No.2 and was insured with respondent No.3 / Insurance Co. on the fateful day.

After evaluating the ocular as well as documentary evidence available on record, the learned tribunal by impugned award has awarded the compensation to the tune of Rs.38,55,436/- in favour of the appellant / claimant as against the claim of Rs.1,50,00,000/-.
Sonu Thru.

sentences.text:
Counsel for the appellant further argued that the tribunal has erred in calculating the amounts in lower side in each and every head.
4.

On the other hand, learned counsel for respondent No.3/ Insurance Co.
supported the impugned award submitting that the learned tribunal has rightly awarded the amount of compensation to the claimant.
He has fairly admitted that the tribunal has erred in not awarding the amount in the head of future prospects.

5. Heard the rival submissions advanced by the learned counsel for the parties and on going through the material and evidence available on record, it is not in dispute that respondent No.1 / driver was responsible for causing accident and offending vehicle was insured with respondent No.3/Insurance Co. on the fateful day.
The only question for determination in this appeal is that the amount of compensation awarded by the claims tribunal is required modification or not ?.

6. Considering the over all facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds that the tribunal has erred in not awarding the amount of compensation on the head of future prospects as per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Pranay Sethi(supra.
Further, this Court finds that the tribunal has NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3439 3 MA-1738-2016 applied multiplier of 12 which should have been 17 looking to the age of injured/claimant.
The claimant is also entitled to get the enhanced compensation under other heads.

Therefore, in view of the above said discussion, the compensation is being recalculated as under :
Income of claimant : Rs 21097 /- per month Annual Income : Rs. 2,53,164/-
Future Prospects (40%) : Rs. 3,54,430/-
Loss of earning capacity (75% disability) : Rs. 2,65,822/- per annum Multiplier (17) :
Rs. 45,18,974/-
Special diet : Rs. 50,000/-
Loss of amenities : Rs. 50,000/-
Pain and Suffering : Rs. 1,00,000/-
transportation : Rs. 20,000/-

Medical Bills : Rs. 1,82,668/-

Further, the tribunal has awarded compensation as Rs. 50,000/- under the head of 'expectancy of life', however, this Court finds that no separate calculation under life expectancy is required once the correct multiplier is applied as same is presumed and built into the multiplier system itself.
Accordingly, the appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation for a sum of Rs.11,96,206/-.
Accordingly, this Court is of the considered opinion that the award passed by the tribunal warranted interference.
The appellant is entitled for enhancement of compensation for a sum of Rs.11,96,206/-.
The enhanced amount shall carry the NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2026:MPHC-IND:3439 4 MA-1738-2016 same interest as has been awarded by the claims tribunal.
Rest of the conditions as imposed by the learned claims tribunal shall remain intact.

7. In view of the aforesaid, the appeal stands partly allowed and the impugned award is modified to the extent as indicated hereinabove subject to the following conditions :-
i.
The respondent-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the compensation amount within 90 days from the date of this order, failing which the execution can be taken out against him.
ii. On the difference amount the appellant would pay the Court fee within one month.
The claimant is directed to pay the requisite Court Fee (if any).
Office is also directed to verify whether any Court Fees is payable for the enhanced compensation amount.
iii. On such deposit, the claimant is permitted to withdraw the amount with accrued interest and costs, by filing a proper application before the Tribunal.
iv. The impugned award of the learned Tribunal stands modified to the aforesaid extent and in terms and directions as above.
v. The record be sent back to the learned Tribunal within three weeks from this day.

(HIMANSHU JOSHI) JUDGE SS/-
Sonu Thru.
